questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Career opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I believe the career opportunities here are much better than UCPH

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very simple, all the information is available on the university’s website

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: During the first few weeks there were several meetings with different university staff members, who showed us all the facilities we would use during the semester and explained how the various web portals we had to use worked.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *

How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found accommodation through friends, so I can’t give other recommendations.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you live off campus, it’s preferable to get a public transport pass to reach campus, or to buy a bicycle (you can find decent ones at a low price).

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Course registration is done through a platform called Ladok. The platform is very intuitive, and you need to register both for the course and for the exam you want to take. Note that in the first study period the International Office handled registration, while from the second period onward registration must be done by the student.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: No real help was provided for that but if necessary, you can contact the International Office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was registered for all the classes I intended to register for

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you have problems with registration, you can contact the GU International Office, they are very kind and usually reply the same day

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All the courses I attended were at the master’s level. The only difficulties I had were related to my background, because (in some courses, but not all) they assumed knowledge I hadn’t covered at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is very similar to UCPH: there are lectures and weekly assignments. In some courses it was also necessary to give presentations

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Computability - DIT313
Programming Language Technology - DIT231
Formal Methods in Software Development - DIT272
Types for Programs and Proofs - DIT235

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I found the course Programming Language Technology particularly interesting, especially for anyone interested in programming languages, because it offers a combination of lectures and assignments that, by the end of the course, give you the knowledge needed to implement your own programming language. 
The course Types for Programs and Proofs provides an introduction to the world of Interactive Theorem Provers (ITPs). The course mainly teaches Agda, software developed at the University of Gothenburg/Chalmers. The course is taught by people who maintain the software and by Prof. Coquand, an important name in the ITP community.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are several student societies at GU. One I participated in was CESAR, a student club that builds rockets for national competitions.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Four times a year, the university organizes social events in which student clubs take part and offer food at very low prices. In addition, there is a building that hosts the student union, where there are several pubs that students usually go to after classes to have a beer or play games

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visiting the city:  Haga, the historic city center; Liseberg, an amusement park; and Universeum, a very nice interactive museum.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It wasn’t difficult because the local culture is similar to the Danish one.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn’t find any challenging differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I especially appreciated how polite and respectful people are and the balance between study/work and personal time.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining at least one student club because, besides being something you can add to your CV, it’s a great way to meet local students.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think it’s essential to participate in all the initial events so you can meet as many people as possible. If you don’t attend these events, there’s a risk that groups will already have formed among students, making it harder to meet new people.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Personally, taking courses taught by professors who are highly experienced and well regarded in academia was an honor for me. Not all universities offer this level of mentorship.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making small talk with other students

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
